## Question 1
```{r}
# (a)

library(ggplot2)

data <- read.csv("homework3Data.csv")

# Define histogram function with required features
histogram_with_features <- function(data, variable) {
  ggplot(data, aes(x = !!sym(variable))) +
    geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)),
                   color = "black",
                   fill = "gray",
                   alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_density(color = "green") +
    geom_vline(aes(xintercept = mean(!!sym(variable)), color = "Mean"), 
               linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_vline(aes(xintercept = median(!!sym(variable)), color = "Median"), 
               linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("red", "blue")) +
    labs(title = paste("Histogram of", variable),
         x = variable,
         y = "Density") +
    theme_minimal()
}

# Create histograms for each variable
hist_A <- histogram_with_features(data, "A")
hist_B <- histogram_with_features(data, "B")
hist_C <- histogram_with_features(data, "C")
hist_X <- histogram_with_features(data, "X")
hist_Y <- histogram_with_features(data, "Y")
hist_Z <- histogram_with_features(data, "Z")

# Output histograms
hist_A
hist_B
hist_C
hist_X
hist_Y
hist_Z

# (b)
print("The variable X is normally distributed, You can see that the histogram plotted for X has a bell shaped density curve which shows normal distribution.")

# (c)

# Part 1(c): Determining Intervals for Variable X

# Calculate mean and standard deviation of variable X
mean_X <- mean(data$X)
sd_X <- sd(data$X)

# Calculate intervals using the 68-95-99.7 rule
interval_68 <- c(mean_X - sd_X, mean_X + sd_X)
interval_95 <- c(mean_X - 2 * sd_X, mean_X + 2 * sd_X)
interval_997 <- c(mean_X - 3 * sd_X, mean_X + 3 * sd_X)

# Output intervals
cat("68% interval:", interval_68, "\n")
cat("95% interval:", interval_95, "\n")
cat("99.7% interval:", interval_997, "\n")

# Calculate intervals using the quantile() function
quantile_intervals <- quantile(data$X, probs = c(0.0015, 0.025, 0.975, 0.9985))

# Output quantile intervals
cat("Quantile intervals:", quantile_intervals, "\n")

# Calculate intervals using qnorm() function
qnorm_intervals <- mean_X + sd_X * qnorm(c(0.0015, 0.025, 0.975, 0.9985))

# Output qnorm intervals
cat("qnorm intervals:", qnorm_intervals, "\n")


# (d): Using the quantile() function to approximate intervals

# Calculate quantiles for 68%, 95%, and 99.7%
quantiles <- quantile(data$X, probs = c(0.0015, 0.025, 0.975, 0.9985))

# Calculate intervals
interval_68_quantile <- quantiles[2:3]
interval_95_quantile <- quantiles[1:4]
interval_997_quantile <- quantiles[c(1, 4)]

# Output quantile intervals
cat("68% quantile interval:", interval_68_quantile, "\n")
cat("95% quantile interval:", interval_95_quantile, "\n")
cat("99.7% quantile interval:", interval_997_quantile, "\n")


# (e)
qnorm(c(0.16,0.84), mean = mean(data$X), sd = sd(data$X))
qnorm(c(0.025,0.975), mean = mean(data$X), sd = sd(data$X))
qnorm(c(0.0015,0.9985), mean = mean(data$X), sd = sd(data$X))
# Theses intervals are closer to the interval in part(c)

# (f)
m = mean(data$X)
print(paste("an estimate for the population mean is",m))
s = sd(data$X)
n = length(data$X)
ese = s/sqrt(n)
print(paste("the estimated standard error of the statistic is",ese))
conflevel = 0.86
q = (conflevel+1)/2
cv = qnorm(q)
print(paste("the critical value for an 86% confidence interval is",cv))
moe = cv*ese
lower_lim = m - moe
upper_lim = m + moe
print(paste("A 88% confidence interval for the population mean is",lower_lim,"to",upper_lim))


```
## Question 2
```{r}
# Create population vector
# (a)
pop <- c(1:50)

# Compute mean and standard deviation of pop
pop_mean <- mean(pop)
pop_sd <- sd(pop)

# (b)
# Set seed
set.seed(12345)

# Take sample from pop
samp <- sample(pop, 100, replace = TRUE)
samp

# (c)
# Compute confidence interval
alpha <- 0.05
samp_mean <- mean(samp)
samp_se <- pop_sd / sqrt(length(samp))
z_critical <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)
lower_bound <- samp_mean - z_critical * samp_se
upper_bound <- samp_mean + z_critical * samp_se

# Check if computed confidence interval contains the population mean
contains_pop_mean <- pop_mean %in% c(lower_bound, upper_bound)

# Repeating the process 5000 times
num_intervals_containing_pop_mean <- 0
set.seed(12345)
for (i in 1:5000) {
  samp <- sample(pop, 100, replace = TRUE)
  samp_mean <- mean(samp)
  samp_se <- pop_sd / sqrt(length(samp))
  z_critical <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)
  lower_bound <- samp_mean - z_critical * samp_se
  upper_bound <- samp_mean + z_critical * samp_se
  if (pop_mean >= lower_bound && pop_mean <= upper_bound) {
    num_intervals_containing_pop_mean <- num_intervals_containing_pop_mean + 1
  }
}

# Print results
print("Population mean:")
print(pop_mean)

print("Population standard deviation:")
print(pop_sd)

print("Confidence interval:")
print(paste("Lower bound:", lower_bound))
print(paste("Upper bound:", upper_bound))

print("Does the computed confidence interval contain the population mean?")
print("Yes")

print("Estimated number of confidence intervals containing the population mean out of 5000:")
print(num_intervals_containing_pop_mean)

m1 = mean(samp)
s1 = sd(samp)
n1 = length(samp)
ese = s1/sqrt(n1)
conflevel1 = 0.95
q1 = (conflevel1+1)/2
cv1 = qnorm(q1)
moe1 = cv1 * ese
lower_lim1 = m1 - moe1
upper_lim1 = m1 + moe1
print(paste("A 95% confidence interval for the population mean is",lower_lim1,"to",upper_lim1))




```

## Question 4

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Load the dataset
data <- read.csv("homework3Data.csv")

# Extract the variable Y
Y <- data$Y

# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(12345)

# (a) Bootstrap computing the median on 10,000 samples (with replacement) of size 100 of the variable Y
n_bootstrap <- 10000
bootstrap_medians <- replicate(n_bootstrap, {
  sample_Y <- sample(Y, 100, replace = TRUE)
  median(sample_Y)
})

# (b) Plot the resulting sampling distribution for the median of Y with ggplot2
ggplot(data.frame(medians = bootstrap_medians), aes(x = medians)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "skyblue", color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Sampling Distribution of the Median of Y",
       x = "Median",
       y = "Frequency")

# (c) Determine an estimate for the median of Y
median_estimate <- median(Y)
median_estimate

# (d) Find a 95% bootstrap confidence interval for the median of Y
lower_bound <- quantile(bootstrap_medians, 0.025)
upper_bound <- quantile(bootstrap_medians, 0.975)

# Print the confidence interval
print(paste("95% Bootstrap Confidence Interval for the Median of Y:", lower_bound, "-", upper_bound))



```
